feature: A typed width shows what the layers took
summary: Type a size the picked layers will not take and the W box now shows the size they actually kept, so the next arrow key steps from a real number. Before this, a button held to a smallest width of 160 sat on the canvas at 160 while W read 50.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to turn on. You need a component or group with a Smallest or Largest width set in the Layout section, which is where a layer gets a rule the fields cannot see in advance.

try.do: Open a blank canvas and drag a Button off the Library shelf onto it.
Click the button, open the chevron beside Width in the Layout section, and type 160 into Smallest.
Click into W in Position & Size, type 50, press Return.
Read W. It says 160, the width the button kept, not the 50 you asked for.
Press the down arrow without leaving the box. It stays 160 rather than counting down from 50.
Read W. A width the button accepts still reads back exactly as typed.

evaluate: When 50 turns into 160 under your hand, does that read as the button refusing, or as the box ignoring you?
The Layout section a few rows below says Smallest 160, so the reason is on screen this time. Is that enough, or should the line under Position & Size say it too?
Is the change instant enough that you never see the 50 you typed sitting in the box?
Do the same three steps feel right on a text label, whose W stops at the width of its own words?
rough: Nothing says WHY the number came back. The pattern doc asks for the reason in the line under the section when a set moves nothing at all, and that half is not built: filed as a-number-that-springs-back-says-why-it-did.

The bug the task described (two labels going to 204 while W read 200) is not a bug. 204 is the stored box, 200 is the words, and the field speaks the words on purpose. The real refusal is a group held by its own flow, which is what this walk and the fix are about.
The screenshots are real screen captures, not offscreen renders: the probe held the Screen Recording grant for this run.
Only Position & Size was fixed. Every other typed number in the dock still shows what it computed rather than what the document took, and nobody has swept them.
